//: Story Phase 2, chapter 2: Garrick's First Day at Sea. Toll line on main-deck row 27 (Garrick at 9,27, sign at 10,27); the galley mess table is (4-6,9).
ch2.begin: hale: Where do you want him, Captain?

choice.text: The galley. Keep him near the food.
then: hale[concerned]: Mags would kill him inside an hour, Captain. Or he'd eat the stores. One or the other.
captain[resigned]: Fine. Not the galley.
hale[smug]: Very good, Captain. Honest work. Wet work.
hale: The foredeck, then. You can't see it from the helm.

ch2.begin: hale: I'll put him on the foredeck with Sully. Swabbing, coiling, the usual. Somebody ought to check he's actually doing it.
hale[smug]: You are the captain, Captain.
ch2.later: An hour later. Charts, coffee and blessed quiet.
wick[concerned]: Captain! You'd better come to the foredeck. The new man's... he's put up a sign.
wick: And a rope. And he's charging people, Captain. Brask had to pay a copper to fetch his own hammer.

ch2.toll_warn.text: Toll deck ahead! Coins ready, please!

ch2.toll_sign.caption: Painted in a hurry on a cupboard door. The paint is still wet.

ch2.toll_confront: garrick[businesslike]: Welcome, valued customer, to Garrick's Toll Deck! One copper to cross the foredeck. Return journeys, two.
captain: A return journey is two crossings.
garrick: Two coppers. Plus a convenience charge.
garrick[smug]: And you're welcome on it, at the captain's rate! Half price. Premium rates apply for loitering, and I must warn you there is a burping surcharge.

then: captain[angry]: Take. It. Down.
garrick[nervous]: Of course! Immediately! As a gesture of goodwill between management and... management.
garrick[businesslike]: Three coppers a burp, Captain. Bob owes me eleven.
captain[laugh]: Bob has never paid for anything in his life.
garrick[offended]: Then he's in ARREARS.
captain: Take it down, Guzzlegut.
captain: Here. One copper.
garrick[delighted]: A pleasure doing business—
captain[smug]: And now it's my copper, on my deck, under my rope. Take it down.
garrick[pretend]: ...I appear to have been out-negotiated.
He hands the copper back. Slowly. As if returning a kidney.

ch2.toll_confront: captain: You're aboard to work. Hale put you on the foredeck. Swabbing.
garrick[businesslike]: Swabbing! Of course. I'm a hands-on sort of executive.
Garrick waddles off in the general direction of the bucket, whistling.
ch2.scrub: Garrick is sitting on an upturned bucket with his boots up, watching Sully scrub around him.
captain: Guzzlegut. What are you doing?
garrick: Every great enterprise needs management. Sully provides the labour. I provide the vision. A little more elbow there, Sully.
sully[annoyed]: Captain, he's been supervising for an hour. He's supervised me scrubbing this one plank four times.

then: captain[angry]: Pick. Up. The brush.

choice.text: Sully, take a break. Garrick scrubs.
then: sully[happy]: Thank you, Captain!
garrick[offended]: This is a demotion.
garrick[delighted]: Thank you! Finally, a man who appreciates results.
captain[annoyed]: Pick up the brush anyway.

ch2.scrub: Garrick picks up the brush and gives the deck one long, magnificent stroke.
garrick[delighted]: Lunch! The most important meeting of the day!
sully: Fastest he's moved all morning, Captain.
captain[annoyed]: Somebody should keep an eye on him in the galley.

start: jim[alarmed]: Captain! Thank the tides. You have to see this. He's been eating for twenty minutes.
garrick[delighted]: Captain! Join me! Your cook is a genius. A tragically underappreciated asset.
jim[annoyed]: I'm not a cook, I'm a PICKLER. And he's eaten half my pickling.
jim: Here. Here's what he's had so far. I've been keeping count.
menu: jim: A whole roasted garlic. Not a clove, Captain. The whole bulb.
garrick[businesslike]: In some cultures garlic is a currency.
jim: Two bowls of cabbage stew.
garrick: Bowls three and four are being held in escrow.
jim[disgusted]: The sour cheese. THE sour cheese. The one we keep in the hold to frighten off rats.
garrick: Robust. Assertive. A cheese with a business plan.
garrick[smug]: The devil drives a hard bargain. So do I.
captain[disgusted]: The ones he paddled here with.
jim: The ones that were in the sea, Captain. For days.
garrick[greedy]: Waste not, Captain. They've been marinating.
jar: garrick: And what's in the jar?
jim[alarmed]: Don't. Don't you touch that jar.

jar.caption: Salty Jim's fermented eel paste. Aged in the forepeak since before Wick was born.

jar: jim: That paste is for rendering. For glue. For killing barnacles off the hull. It is NOT for eating.
jim[angry]: And it is NOT to be opened below deck. It says so ON THE JAR.
garrick[businesslike]: Warnings like that are a negotiating position.
garrick[delighted]: Mmm! Notes of low tide. A hint of regret. Lingering finish.
jim[disgusted]: He ate it. He ate the whole jar.
jim[alarmed]: Captain, a SPOONFUL of that clears a bilge.
rumble: Every head in the galley turns, slowly, toward Garrick.
garrick[nervous]: ...Hull settling. Old ships. They talk.
garrick[pretend]: Well! Back to work. The sails won't supervise themselves.
jim[concerned]: Captain. A word. When you've got a moment.

ch2.jim_warning: jim[concerned]: I've been pickling thirty years, Captain. I know what food does to a man.
jim: Twelve onions, a garlic, the cheese, the eggs, the beans, a pair of sea-soaked sausages... and a jar of fermented eel. All in one sitting.
jim[alarmed]: And it's all got to go SOMEWHERE, Captain.

then: jim: When I was a boy, a man in Port Farthing ate half a jar of that paste.
jim[disgusted]: They had to burn the tavern. Then they had to burn the ashes.

choice.text: I'll keep an eye on him.
then: jim: Keep both eyes on him, Captain. And a nose.

choice.text: Why did you even MAKE that paste?
then: jim[annoyed]: For the hull! One dab and every barnacle within a fathom lets go and swims for it.
jim[concerned]: And now it's inside a man.

ch2.jim_warning: jim: Keep him above deck, in the open air. And for pity's sake keep him away from anything you'd like to keep.
ch2.sail_rumble: Garrick is 'helping' Rook with the mainsail. Rook is doing the pulling. Garrick is doing the grunting.
garrick[businesslike]: Heaving! Heaving in an advisory capacity!
rook: Captain, I don't think that came from the mast.
ch2.thunder: captain: Guzzlegut. What was that noise?
captain: There isn't a cloud in the sky.
garrick: Distant thunder. Very distant. Other side of the world. Dreadful weather over there, I hear.

then: garrick[offended]: Captain! I'll have you know my stomach is a well-regulated institution.
garrick[nervous]: ...That was a seagull.
captain: Thunder.
garrick[relieved]: Thunder!
captain: Distant.
garrick: Tremendously distant.
garrick[businesslike]: Doctors, Captain, are an unnecessary overhead.
garrick: My body is a self-regulating market.
